extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in quantum algebra and algebraic topology; readers of arXiv paper metadata
extracted.subtask_description: Metadata, abstract, comments, and version/withdrawal information for a single mathematics research paper (arXiv:0710.3550) about Frobenius properads and differential forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct definition of the Frobenius properad
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition given for the Frobenius properad is incorrect, i.e. what is stated is not a properad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states this as the substantive error motivating withdrawal; a correct treatment requires a proper definition of the Frobenius properad before downstream constructions/claims can be trusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign conventions and permutation group actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For sign reasons following from the permutation group actions, in odd degree n, there should be no positive genus operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign and symmetry considerations (permutation-group actions) impose structural constraints (e.g., absence of positive genus operations in odd degree) that must be respected in definitions and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence of theorem validity on correct definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The error in that definition invalidates the proof of the main claim in Theorem 4 (even for a proper definition of Frobenius properad). Theorem 8 is also affected similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When foundational definitions are incorrect, proofs of main results may be invalidated; authors/reviewers must check that the definitions used legitimately support the theorems claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper status and licensing when withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper has been withdrawn by the author. No license for this version due to withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata about withdrawal and licensing affects availability and citation: withdrawn papers may still be viewable but should be treated as containing acknowledged errors; check version history and author comments.
